the-joe-rogan-experience.overview:
Most podcasts are edited into a tidy package. This one mostly isn't. Joe Rogan, a stand-up comedian who also works as a UFC commentator, sits down with a guest and lets the conversation run, often for two or three hours, sometimes longer. The guest list is deliberately all over the place: scientists, fighters, comics, authors, politicians, people with strange hobbies.

That looseness is the appeal and the criticism in one. You get long answers and tangents you would never hear in a ten-minute TV slot, and you also get plenty of episodes where a claim goes unchallenged. Treat it as a conversation to listen to, not a fact-check.

It has been running since 2009, which makes it one of the longer-lived shows in this list, and it is the one most people mean when they say 'the biggest podcast in the world' in casual conversation.
the-joe-rogan-experience.format: One host, one guest, unscripted, usually 2 to 3 hours
the-joe-rogan-experience.best_for: Listeners who like long, wandering interviews and do not mind sitting with a view they may disagree with.

faq.q: Who hosts The Joe Rogan Experience?
faq.a: Joe Rogan, a comedian and UFC commentator, hosts every episode.

faq.q: How long is a typical episode?
faq.a: Usually between two and three hours, and some run longer.

hosts.name: Joe Rogan
hosts.bio: An American comedian, actor and former television host who also works as a UFC commentator. He started the podcast in December 2009 on YouTube with the comedian Brian Redban, who co-hosted and produced it until 2012.

the-daily.overview:
The Daily does one thing: it takes the biggest story of the day and spends about half an hour on it. The New York Times reporter closest to the story usually joins the host, Michael Barbaro or a colleague, and walks through what happened and why it matters.

It is built for people who see the headline and want the background without reading five articles. Episodes go up on weekday mornings in the US, so the show works well as a commute companion.

Because it comes from a newsroom, the reporting is sourced and the episodes are tied to published Times stories, which you can read afterwards if you want the detail.
the-daily.format: Host plus a reporter, one story per episode, roughly 20 to 30 minutes
the-daily.best_for: People who want one story explained properly rather than a headline roundup.

faq.a: The New York Times.

faq.q: Does it cover more than one story an episode?
faq.a: Mostly no. Each episode is built around a single story.

hosts.name: Michael Barbaro
hosts.bio: An American journalist and the show's founding host. The Daily now also has other hosts, including Rachel Abrams and Natalie Kitroeff.

call-her-daddy.overview:
Call Her Daddy began in 2018 as a two-host show about dating and sex, and has since turned into something closer to a celebrity interview series. Alex Cooper now hosts on her own.

The tone is conversational and often personal. Guests are pushed on their private lives more than their latest project, which is why the show sits in our culture category rather than entertainment news.

If you want a straight news podcast, this is not it. If you want to hear how a famous person talks when the questions are about them, it is a good place to start.
call-her-daddy.best_for: Pop-culture listeners who prefer personal conversation over promotional interviews.

faq.a: Alex Cooper. The show began with two hosts and has been hosted by Cooper alone for some years now.

hosts.name: Alex Cooper
hosts.bio: Co-created the show with Sofia Franklyn in 2018. Franklyn left in 2020 after a public dispute with the show's then owner, Barstool Sports, and Cooper carried on alone. In 2021 she signed an exclusive deal with Spotify.

crime-junkie.overview:
Two friends, Ashley Flowers and Brit Prince, take a case and tell it from beginning to end in a single episode. Most of the cases are murders and disappearances, and many are unsolved.

It is produced by audiochuck, Flowers' own company, and that helps explain the steady weekly rhythm and the polished storytelling. Expect a lot of context on the victim, not only the crime, and regular calls for listeners with information to come forward.

It is heavy material. If you are new to true crime, pick an older, resolved case first and see whether the format suits you.

The show is based in Indianapolis, Indiana.
crime-junkie.format: Two hosts, one case per episode, narrated
crime-junkie.best_for: True-crime listeners who like a clear beginning, middle and end.

faq.a: It is produced by audiochuck and hosted by Ashley Flowers and Brit Prince.

hosts.name: Ashley Flowers
hosts.bio: An American podcaster, writer and entrepreneur who created the show. Her debut novel, All Good People Here, became a New York Times bestseller in 2022.

hosts.name: Brit Prince
hosts.bio: Co-host of the show, credited in some reference sources under her name Brit Prawat.

the-mel-robbins-podcast.overview:
Mel Robbins is known as the author of The 5 Second Rule, and her podcast is that idea stretched into a full show: practical, direct advice about motivation, confidence and small habits you can actually start today.

Episodes mix solo talks with conversations with experts in psychology and health. The delivery is blunt and encouraging rather than academic, so the value is in the specific things she asks you to try, not in the theory behind them.

If you are already deep into self-help books you may hear familiar ideas. If you are not, it is an easy way in.
the-mel-robbins-podcast.best_for: People who want short, actionable advice more than research deep-dives.

faq.q: What is Mel Robbins best known for?
faq.a: Her book The 5 Second Rule and her work as a speaker on motivation.

hosts.name: Mel Robbins
hosts.bio: An American author, podcast host and lawyer, best known for her book The 5 Second Rule.

huberman-lab.overview:
Andrew Huberman is a professor of neurobiology and ophthalmology at Stanford, and the podcast is where he explains how the brain and body work in plain language: sleep, focus, stress, exercise, vision.

Episodes are long. A solo episode can run well over an hour, and interviews with other scientists go longer. The format is closer to a lecture than a chat, and he tends to end with concrete protocols people can try.

As with any health podcast, treat it as an introduction. Findings are simplified, and anything that affects your medical care should go through a doctor.

Some scientists have criticised him for promoting supplements and for health claims with limited evidence, so it is worth treating individual claims with the same care you would any single source.
huberman-lab.format: Long solo lectures and expert interviews
huberman-lab.best_for: Listeners who like detailed explanations of how the body works.

faq.a: A professor of neurobiology and ophthalmology at Stanford University who hosts the show.

hosts.name: Andrew Huberman
hosts.bio: An American neuroscientist and an associate professor of neurobiology and ophthalmology at the Stanford University School of Medicine. He has hosted the show since 2021.

this-american-life.overview:
This American Life started as a public radio show in Chicago in 1995 and is still built the same way: each week has a theme, and the hour is made of several true stories that fit it, some funny, some hard to hear.

Ira Glass hosts and narrates between the stories. The production values are the reason the show is studied by people who make audio: the writing is careful, and the pacing is deliberate.

It is a good first stop if you want storytelling rather than interviews, and its back catalogue is deep enough to listen to for months.

The first episode aired on 17 November 1995 under a different title, Your Radio Playhouse, before the show took its current name.
this-american-life.format: Themed hour, several stories per episode
this-american-life.best_for: Anyone who likes well-crafted true stories.

faq.q: Where did This American Life start?
faq.a: On public radio in Chicago, in 1995, before it became a widely downloaded podcast.

hosts.name: Ira Glass
hosts.bio: An American public-radio host and producer. Before the show he worked on NPR programmes including Morning Edition and All Things Considered, and his work has won awards such as the George Polk Award.

armchair-expert.overview:
Dax Shepard is an actor, and his interview show is built on the idea that everyone is an expert at something. He and co-host Monica Padman talk to actors, writers, scientists and other guests, usually for well over an hour.

The interviews start with the guest's childhood and work forward, which is why they often feel more personal than a typical promotional chat. Shepard is open about his own history, and guests tend to match that honesty.

It is chatty and long. If you want tight and fast, look elsewhere.
armchair-expert.format: Host and co-host interview one guest
armchair-expert.best_for: Fans of long, personal celebrity interviews.

faq.a: Dax Shepard, with co-host Monica Padman.

hosts.name: Dax Shepard
hosts.bio: An American actor, comedian and filmmaker who has hosted the show since it premiered on 14 February 2018. His first guest was his wife, the actor Kristen Bell.

hosts.name: Monica Padman
hosts.bio: An American podcaster, actor and producer who co-created the show and co-hosts it. Her acting credits include The Good Place.

stuff-you-should-know.overview:
Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant have been explaining how things work since 2008: everything from everyday objects to historical events to scientific ideas. Topics are picked from curiosity, not the news.

The two hosts research the topic, then talk it through with jokes and asides. Episodes are usually under an hour, and you come away knowing a little about a lot.

It is a good background listen: no need to follow a storyline, and you can start with any episode.
stuff-you-should-know.format: Two hosts, one topic per episode
stuff-you-should-know.best_for: Curious listeners who like learning something new in under an hour.

faq.q: Who hosts Stuff You Should Know?
faq.a: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant.

hosts.name: Josh Clark
hosts.bio: Co-host since the show launched in 2008. It was originally published by HowStuffWorks.

hosts.name: Chuck Bryant
hosts.bio: Charles W. Bryant, the other co-host since the launch in 2008.

my-favorite-murder.overview:
Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark each bring a true-crime story to the table and tell it to the other. It began in 2016 and helped make comedic true crime popular.

What makes it work is the tone: two friends, obviously fans of the genre, talking about dark subjects with humour and, often, real care for the people involved. Listeners send in their own stories, which the show has also featured.

It is a different experience from the more serious, narrated shows in this category, and not for people who dislike jokes in true crime.
my-favorite-murder.best_for: Listeners who want true crime with humour.

faq.a: Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark.

hosts.name: Karen Kilgariff
hosts.bio: An American comedian, writer and actor who started in stand-up in the early 1990s. She was in the cast of Mr. Show and has written for several TV shows.

hosts.name: Georgia Hardstark
hosts.bio: An American television host and podcast personality. In 2018 she and Kilgariff co-founded the Exactly Right podcast network, and in 2019 they published a joint memoir.

the-diary-of-a-ceo.overview:
Steven Bartlett built a social media marketing company, Social Chain, before he started this podcast, and it shows in the guests: founders, doctors, authors and psychologists, often talking about how they run their lives and businesses.

The interviews are long and the questions are personal. Bartlett tends to ask about a guest's low points as much as their wins, which is why it is popular with people who want business stories with a human side.

It is one of the most listened-to British shows, and a recognisable route into the UK's business-podcast scene.
the-diary-of-a-ceo.format: One host, one guest, long interviews
the-diary-of-a-ceo.best_for: Ambitious listeners who like founder and expert interviews with personal detail.

faq.q: Who hosts The Diary of a CEO?
faq.a: Steven Bartlett, a British entrepreneur.

hosts.name: Steven Bartlett
hosts.bio: A British businessman, investor and podcaster. The first episode came out on 29 September 2017, with the fellow chief executive Mark Stringer as the first guest.

sources.label: Wikipedia: The Diary of a CEO

the-rest-is-politics.overview:
Alastair Campbell worked as Tony Blair's communications chief. Rory Stewart was a Conservative MP and a government minister. They disagree on plenty, and that is the point of the show.

Twice a week they take apart what is happening in British and world politics: not a party line from either of them, and generally more candid than a broadcast panel show. Their inside knowledge of how government actually works is the real draw.

Its success also led to a family of 'Rest Is...' shows from the same production company, Goalhanger.
the-rest-is-politics.format: Two hosts, conversation, no guests most weeks
the-rest-is-politics.best_for: Followers of UK and international politics who want two experienced voices.

faq.q: Who are the hosts of The Rest Is Politics?
faq.a: Alastair Campbell, a former Labour communications chief, and Rory Stewart, a former Conservative minister.

hosts.name: Alastair Campbell
hosts.bio: A British journalist, author and strategist. He was Tony Blair's spokesman and campaign director in opposition, then Downing Street press secretary and director of communications.

hosts.name: Rory Stewart
hosts.bio: A British academic, broadcaster, writer and former diplomat and politician. He was the Conservative MP for Penrith and The Border and is a professor in practice at the London School of Economics.

the-rest-is-history.overview:
Tom Holland writes popular history books and Dominic Sandbrook is a historian and broadcaster. Together they tell stories from history in a way that is closer to a good dinner conversation than a lecture.

They will spend a run of episodes on a single subject, such as an empire or a war, which lets them go into more depth than the typical one-off episode. Their differences of opinion keep it lively.

If you liked school history but felt it skipped the interesting parts, this is aimed at you.
the-rest-is-history.format: Two historians in conversation, often in multi-part series
the-rest-is-history.best_for: Listeners who like history told as stories.

faq.q: Who hosts The Rest Is History?
faq.a: Historians Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook.

hosts.name: Tom Holland
hosts.bio: A British novelist and popular historian.

hosts.name: Dominic Sandbrook
hosts.bio: A British historian, author, columnist and television presenter. He has co-hosted the show since 2020.

the-news-agents.overview:
Three experienced British journalists, Emily Maitlis, Jon Sopel and Lewis Goodall, moved from broadcast news to a daily podcast, and the background shows: the focus is on what is happening and why, with reporters' instincts intact.

It is produced by Global and launched on 30 August 2022, with a new episode every weekday afternoon. Each episode usually centres on one main story, plus interviews with people close to it.

It suits UK news followers who want reporters, not commentators, walking through the day.
the-news-agents.format: Three presenters, a lead story and interviews
the-news-agents.best_for: UK news followers who want a daily briefing.

faq.a: Emily Maitlis, Jon Sopel and Lewis Goodall.

hosts.name: Emily Maitlis
hosts.bio: A British journalist who was the lead anchor of BBC Two's Newsnight from 2018 to the end of 2021.

hosts.name: Jon Sopel
hosts.bio: A British journalist and presenter, formerly the BBC's North America editor and chief political correspondent.

hosts.name: Lewis Goodall
hosts.bio: A British journalist, broadcaster and author, formerly a political correspondent at Sky News and policy editor of Newsnight.

the-rest-is-football.overview:
Gary Lineker is joined by Alan Shearer and Micah Richards, two former professional players, to talk about the game. An experienced presenter plus two people who have played at the top level gives it a different feel from a studio panel of journalists.

It launched in August 2023 from Goalhanger, the company behind The Rest Is Politics and The Rest Is History, and has since grown from audio into video and television. The mix is news, match talk and a lot of banter.

It is best when there is plenty going on in the English game. Expect conversation more than tactics diagrams.
the-rest-is-football.frequency: Several episodes a week in season
the-rest-is-football.format: Three presenters, football talk and banter
the-rest-is-football.best_for: Football fans, especially of the English game, who want conversation more than tactics diagrams.

faq.q: Who is on The Rest Is Football?
faq.a: Gary Lineker, Alan Shearer and Micah Richards.

hosts.name: Gary Lineker
hosts.bio: A former England striker with 80 caps and now a broadcaster. He is the only player to have finished as top scorer in England with three clubs: Leicester City, Everton and Tottenham Hotspur.

hosts.name: Alan Shearer
hosts.bio: A former striker and now a football pundit, and the Premier League's record goalscorer with 260 goals.

hosts.name: Micah Richards
hosts.bio: A former right-back and now a football pundit.

off-menu.overview:
Ed Gamble and James Acaster both work as stand-up comedians. Their show gives each guest a genie's offer: one starter, one main, one side, one dessert, one drink, and the meal they would order if they could have anything.

Everything hangs on the small stuff: where a guest's favourite food comes from, what they hate, and the disagreements that follow. It is silly, and it is meant to be.

Because the format is fixed, you can start with any episode; pick a guest you like.
off-menu.format: Two comedians, one guest, a dream meal
off-menu.best_for: Comedy fans and people who enjoy talking about food.

faq.a: Comedians Ed Gamble and James Acaster.

hosts.name: Ed Gamble
hosts.bio: An English comedian and podcaster, known for panel shows including Mock the Week and Taskmaster. He started out performing with the Durham Revue at Durham University.

hosts.name: James Acaster
hosts.bio: An English comedian, presenter and musician, known for stand-up specials including Repertoire and Cold Lasagne Hate Myself 1999.

table-manners.overview:
Jessie Ware, a singer, hosts alongside her mother, Lennie, and every episode is recorded at Jessie's dining table with a guest, over a meal.

The result is warmer and slower than a normal celebrity interview: the questions are family-style and the food is part of the conversation. Lennie's interventions are often the best part.

It is a gentle, funny listen and a good fit for a weekend.
table-manners.format: A meal with a guest, hosted by mother and daughter
table-manners.best_for: Listeners who like cosy, food-led conversation.

faq.a: Singer Jessie Ware and her mother, Lennie Ware.

hosts.name: Jessie Ware
hosts.bio: A British singer and songwriter, whose debut album, Devotion, came out in 2012.

hosts.name: Lennie Ware
hosts.bio: Jessie's mother and co-host, who joins in on every episode.

desert-island-discs.overview:
One of the longest-running radio programmes in the world, Desert Island Discs began in 1942. The idea has hardly changed: a guest imagines being cast away on a desert island and chooses eight records, a book and a luxury to take with them.

The music is a way into their life story: why that song, and what was happening when they first heard it. It has been presented by a series of hosts over the decades; Lauren Laverne has hosted since 2018.

It is on BBC Radio 4, which also makes a large archive available online.
desert-island-discs.format: One guest, eight records, a book and a luxury
desert-island-discs.best_for: Anyone who enjoys a life story told through music.

faq.q: Who presents Desert Island Discs now?
faq.a: Lauren Laverne, since 2018.
Eight pieces of music, one book and one luxury item.

hosts.name: Lauren Laverne
hosts.bio: An English radio and television presenter, author and singer. She was previously the lead singer and guitarist of the band Kenickie. The programme itself first went out on 29 January 1942.

in-our-time.overview:
A programme on BBC Radio 4 that takes a single big subject, such as a historical figure, a scientific idea or a work of literature, and puts three academics in a room to discuss it for about forty-five minutes.

It has been running since 1998 and was presented for most of that time by Melvyn Bragg. The format has been consistent: a short introduction, a discussion led by the presenter, and a tight schedule.

The archive is the value here. It covers an enormous range of subjects, and it is a good way to get a solid overview of a topic from people who teach it.
in-our-time.format: Presenter and three academics, one topic
in-our-time.best_for: Curious listeners who want an expert-led overview.

faq.q: Which broadcaster makes In Our Time?
faq.a: BBC Radio 4.

hosts.name: Melvyn Bragg
hosts.bio: An English broadcaster, author and member of the House of Lords. He presented Start the Week on Radio 4 from 1988 and edited and presented The South Bank Show. In Our Time first aired in October 1998 and passed its 1,000th episode in September 2023.

the-adam-buxton-podcast.overview:
Adam Buxton is a British comedian, formerly of the double act Adam and Joe. His podcast is a series of long, relaxed conversations with writers, musicians, comedians and others, which often wander off topic.

He also reads out messages and reflections from listeners. It has a more homemade feel than the polished shows in this list, and that is its charm.

A good fit for people who prefer talk that takes its time.
the-adam-buxton-podcast.best_for: Listeners who like gentle, funny, meandering conversation.

faq.a: A British comedian who was half of the double act Adam and Joe.

hosts.name: Adam Buxton
hosts.bio: An English comedian, podcaster and actor. With the filmmaker Joe Cornish he is half of Adam and Joe, who made The Adam and Joe Show for Channel 4 (1996 to 2001). The podcast's first episode came out in 2015.

the-ranveer-show.overview:
Ranveer Allahbadia is a creator who became widely known online under the name BeerBiceps, and The Ranveer Show is his interview series. The conversations cover business, fitness, spirituality and personal growth, with guests from across India.

It runs in Hindi and English, which is part of why it reaches a wide audience. The interviews are long and conversational, and he tends to ask about how a guest thinks as much as what they have done.

It is a useful window into how a large part of India's young online audience thinks about success and self-improvement.
the-ranveer-show.best_for: Listeners who want Indian founders and public figures in long-form conversation.

faq.q: Which languages does The Ranveer Show use?
faq.a: Hindi and English.

hosts.name: Ranveer Allahbadia
hosts.bio: An Indian content creator, widely known online as BeerBiceps.

figuring-out-with-raj-shamani.overview:
Raj Shamani is an entrepreneur and content creator, and Figuring Out is his interview series. He talks to founders, creators and other public figures about how they got where they are.

Episodes are conversational and aimed at people who are building something: a business, a following, a career. Questions tend to be practical, such as what worked, what did not, and how they made decisions.

It is broadcast largely in Hindi with some English.
figuring-out-with-raj-shamani.format: Interviews, mostly Hindi with some English

faq.a: Raj Shamani, an entrepreneur and content creator.

hosts.name: Raj Shamani
hosts.bio: An Indian entrepreneur and podcaster, best known for hosting this show.

wtf-is-with-nikhil-kamath.overview:
Nikhil Kamath co-founded the stockbroker Zerodha with his brother, and is an investor. His podcast is a series of open conversations with business leaders, founders and other well-known guests.

The show is built around him asking the questions he wants answered about how a business works, and how money and technology are changing. It is conversational and in English.

It is a useful listen for people who follow Indian business.
wtf-is-with-nikhil-kamath.best_for: Followers of Indian business and startups.

faq.a: A co-founder of the stockbroker Zerodha and an investor.

hosts.name: Nikhil Kamath
hosts.bio: An Indian entrepreneur and investor. He co-founded the stockbroker Zerodha, with his brother Nithin, and the asset manager True Beacon.

the-seen-and-the-unseen.overview:
Amit Varma, a writer who ran the blog India Uncut, hosts long conversations about Indian society, economics, culture and ideas. Guests include academics, writers and practitioners.

The show is unhurried. Episodes often go two hours or more and tend to go deep on one subject, which makes it a reference for listeners who want to understand the thinking behind policy and culture debates.

It leans towards classical liberal ideas, and Varma is open about his own views.
the-seen-and-the-unseen.best_for: Readers and listeners who want depth on Indian ideas and policy.

faq.q: Who hosts The Seen and the Unseen?
faq.a: Amit Varma, a writer.

hosts.name: Amit Varma
hosts.bio: A writer and podcaster based in Mumbai.

cyrus-says.overview:
Cyrus Broacha is a well-known Indian humorist and television presenter. On Cyrus Says he interviews public figures from politics, film, media and sport, with jokes never far from the surface.

It is more light-hearted than most of the podcasts in this list, and it helps that his guests often relax into the conversation. Expect gentle teasing and fewer deep dives.

It is an easy first listen for those who prefer a laugh with their interviews.
cyrus-says.best_for: Listeners who like humour with their interviews.

faq.a: Cyrus Broacha, a humorist and television presenter.

hosts.name: Cyrus Broacha
hosts.bio: An Indian anchor, comedian, political satirist, columnist and author. He is best known for the show Bakra on MTV India and The Week That Wasn't on CNN-News18.

puliyabaazi.overview:
Puliyabaazi is one of the better-known Hindi-language podcasts on public policy, economics and society. Saurabh Chandra hosts conversations that go into subjects in more detail than a news bulletin allows.

The value is in the language as much as the topics: policy discussion in Hindi is still much rarer than in English, so the show reaches listeners who are underserved elsewhere.

It suits people who want depth, and are happy to listen slowly.
puliyabaazi.best_for: Hindi speakers interested in policy and economics.

faq.a: Hindi.

hosts.name: Saurabh Chandra
hosts.bio: Host of the show.

ideas-of-india.overview:
Ideas of India is hosted by the economist Shruti Rajagopalan. Each episode is an interview about Indian economics, politics or public policy, with academics and practitioners from India and abroad.

The conversations are technical in places, but the host is good at pulling out the point. It is a good route into the arguments behind Indian economic policy.

It is in English and suits readers of policy debate.
ideas-of-india.best_for: Readers interested in Indian economics and governance.

faq.a: The economist Shruti Rajagopalan.

hosts.name: Shruti Rajagopalan
hosts.bio: An economist who hosts the show.

unfiltered-by-samdish.overview:
Samdish Bhatia is a content creator, and Unfiltered is his interview show with entertainers, athletes and other Indian public figures. The tone is casual and question-led.

Guests are drawn from film, television, sport and online media, and episodes are recorded in a mix of Hindi and English.

It fits people who follow Indian entertainment and want more personality than a formal interview offers.
unfiltered-by-samdish.best_for: Followers of Indian film, TV and creators.

faq.a: Samdish Bhatia, a content creator.

hosts.name: Samdish Bhatia
hosts.bio: An Indian content creator who hosts the show.

yaadon-ka-idiot-box.overview:
Neelesh Misra is a lyricist, writer and radio host, and this show is his storytelling series in Hindi. Stories and memories are told in his voice, often with music, and many are about ordinary people's lives.

Storytelling in Hindi audio has a long tradition on Indian radio, and this show is a modern take on it. It is more about atmosphere and feeling than plot.

It suits listeners who like stories rather than talk.

faq.a: Neelesh Misra, a writer, lyricist and radio host.

hosts.name: Neelesh Misra
hosts.bio: An Indian journalist, author, radio storyteller, scriptwriter and lyricist. He hosted Yaadon Ka IdiotBox on BIG FM 92.7 and co-founded the rural newspaper Gaon Connection.

orbital-gadgets-360.overview:
Orbital is the technology podcast from NDTV's Gadgets 360, the Indian tech news outlet. The show covers the week's phone, gadget and tech-industry news from an Indian point of view.

That local angle is the reason to listen: launches, prices and policies are discussed as they apply to buyers in India, not just as global headlines.

It is short enough to fit into a commute and is a good companion to the site's reviews.
orbital-gadgets-360.format: Conversation on the week in tech, in English
orbital-gadgets-360.best_for: Indian buyers and followers of gadgets and tech.

faq.a: NDTV Gadgets 360.
